items_missed: No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse benefit is completely absent. He listed 'insurance' as included in the rate and never said what it actually covers.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned.
No 60 cents per pound baseline contrast — the whole insurance differentiator went unexplained.

No agenda timeframe and no 'sound good?' — the roadmap was strong ('I'm gonna grab some missing information, after that I can go straight into pricing') but there was no 10-15 minute expectation set and no ask for confirmation.
Never used the customer's name once in the entire call, and never confirmed he had the right person on an outbound call.
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops.
No elevator, parking, loading-zone, gate-code or apartment-office questions — on an apartment-to-apartment move with second-floor units at both ends, that access gap can cost real time on move day.
No open-ended stressor question — 'anything you're concerned about moving?' was scoped narrowly to antiques and gun safes, not the move overall.
Never asked about narrow hallways or tight turns.

Quoted $206 as a flat hourly rate without ever saying per mover per hour. The number is right for a two-mover crew, but the customer can't compare it to a competitor's per-mover quote and can't reason about what a third mover would cost.

Zero Save Your Ass content — and the opening was handed to him. The customer said 'I will have everything ready' and 'I should be good with most of the packing before the movers arrived,' which is the exact cue for the prep-equals-lower-bill speech. No consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip, no close.

No full no-hidden-fees pitch — he got no cancellation fees, no rescheduling fees and no card to hold, but never the no credit card fees / no transportation fees / no fuel surcharge / no assembly fees run.
Talked over the customer's question. She started 'Yeah, can you?' and he came in with 'And then we do book up. Yeah, I'm gonna follow up with that next.' The question never got asked.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' — closed the call cold right after the booking objection.
No 'reply with any corrections' ask, which matters more than usual here because she is reviewing the estimate unsupervised.
No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email.
Never gave business hours or how to reach us.
No equivalents or reference points to make the time range concrete.
No Ecobox or Sparefoot mention, though no storage need surfaced.
top_strength: The estimate discipline is the best thing on either of this week's calls and it is exactly the behavior the 52-percent accuracy problem needs. He built the quote off a real room-by-room inventory rather than square footage — master bedroom, second bedroom, living room, dining, bar stools, patio and garage — and probed at the level that actually changes load time, asking whether the bed frame was 'basic headboard foot board slats or any like underneath storage' and pinning down the IKEA Kallax units as 'the one by four the long ones.' He then adjusted live and said so out loud: 'let me adjust my estimate real quick, I was assuming we're doing packing.' Best moment of the call: he gave the 3.5-to-5.5-hour range, then deliberately anchored high with stated reasoning — 'I would keep you at the high end of that range at 5.5 just to set proper expectations. And my reasoning behind that is we are coming from the second floor unit with stair access, making about a thirty minute drive to the new location, stair access again, boxes sound typical' — and closed with 'our goal is to always beat the estimate.' That is conservative anchoring with the variables named, and the math checks out at $206 times 5.5 equals the $1,133 he quoted. He also volunteered the day-rate tiers unprompted before being asked about price, and ran all of this in 7.4 minutes.
coaching_note: Chris, this is a well-run call that forgot to sell Einstein. Highest-leverage fix: you skipped all three differentiators. No No Worries, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee — and you said the word 'insurance' as a throwaway inside the inclusions list, which is the worst version of it, because now she thinks she's been told about coverage when she hasn't. Right after the inclusions, that needed to be: 'and three things that come with every move — No Worries Damage Coverage, up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse, where most companies only give you the state-mandated 60 cents a pound; Meet Your Mover, an email a few days out with your mover's photo so you know who's at your door; and our On-Time Guarantee, if we miss the window we start discounting immediately.' That's forty seconds and it's the whole reason to pick us. It matters more than usual on this call because she declined to book and is going to sit with your estimate next to somebody else's — right now the only thing distinguishing you in that comparison is the number, and you're not the cheapest. Second priority: Save Your Ass, which she teed up for you when she said she'd have everything ready before the movers arrive. The answer there is 'that's great, and here's how to make it pay off — loose items out of drawers, photos off the walls, kids' toys consolidated, and take a carload of the small stuff yourself. You're paying by the hour, so every one of those comes off your bill. Make sense?' Third, smaller but fix it: she started to ask you something with 'Yeah, can you?' and you talked over her, then closed without ever asking if she had questions. When she declined the booking you recovered well with no cancellation fees and no card needed — that was a good instinct — but pair it next time with 'what would you want to see to feel good about locking it in?' and use her name at least three times. You never said it once.
phone_presence_notes: Efficient, confident and professional with the customer responding positively throughout ('sounds good' three times), but purely transactional — zero name use, no empathy or warmth markers, and he talked over her one attempt to ask a question.
